extracted.intended_audience: American short-story authors, magazine contributors, and editors/anthologists using a 1917 yearbook of short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: A yearbook page listing addresses of American magazines that publish short stories and a 'Roll of Honor' of notable short stories/authors for 1917 (with notation conventions). Useful for authors seeking publication venues and for understanding the anthology's selection notations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address list scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. This address list does not aim to be complete, but is based simply on the magazines which I have considered for this volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that the following list is selective (editor/author's consideration set) rather than exhaustive; users should not treat it as a complete directory of all markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses of American magazines publishing short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Ainslee's Magazine, 79 Seventh Avenue, New York City; All-Story Weekly, 8 West 40th Street, New York City; American Magazine, 381 Fourth Avenue, New York City; ... Youth's Companion, St. Paul Street, Boston, Mass. (full list of magazines and street addresses follows)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete publication venues and mailing addresses for submitting short stories or researching where short fiction was being published in 1917. The list is presented as the editor's considered set (see Address list scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality restriction for Roll of Honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. Only stories by American authors are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biographical Roll of Honor and listings that follow include only American-authored stories; non-American authors are therefore excluded from this curated Roll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for top selections (best sixty-three)
rubrics_metrics.description: The best sixty-three stories are indicated by an asterisk before the title of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An asterisk next to a story title marks it as one of the 'best sixty-three' as judged for this Roll of Honor; readers can use this notation to identify the editor's top selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for repeat inclusion in past Rolls
rubrics_metrics.description: The index figures 1, 2, and 3 prefixed to the name of the author indicate that his work has been included in the Rolls of Honor for 1914, 1915, and 1916 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric prefixes (1, 2, 3) by author names denote prior recognition in earlier Rolls of Honor (1914–1916), signalling recurring distinction or continued editorial favor.
